tagline: Tariff swings, electric trucks that don't pencil yet, software on the road.

kpis.l: Q3 2025 sales drop, then Q1 2026 orders
trucks touched by one over-the-air fix

lead_thesis: DTNA's market swings from a 39% sales drop to an 85% order surge while tariffs and charging gaps reshape the business.
lead_support: Pre-buy means customers ordering early to beat price hikes, which distorts demand. TCO is total cost to own and run a truck. The fix: strip noise from forecasts and track every truck in the field.

problems.heading: A 25% truck tariff flipped sales from −39% to +85% orders
problems.fact: Profit halved by May 2026 on tariffs and weak demand; by August 2026 guidance was raised as buyers ordered ahead of price hikes.

calls.heading: Strip pre-buy noise from the order book
Price tariffs into every quote, weekly
Speed up the US plant — own the tariff math
Rent trucks by the mile
calls.sub: Earn on freight cycles, not sales cycles.

problems.heading: Electric trucks work — the chargers don't
problems.fact: The CEO calls the charger shortage a top concern; Greenlane added a second charging corridor in August 2025, but coverage gaps and depot costs remain.

calls.heading: Publish range and cost per route from telemetry
Bundle chargers with every e-truck quote
calls.sub: No sale without a place to plug in.

calls.heading: Fund 20 company charging depots
calls.sub: Own the bottleneck; sell the fuel.

calls.heading: Lease batteries for life, sell miles
calls.sub: Recurring revenue like a phone plan.

problems.heading: One software fix touched 330,000 trucks in the field
problems.fact: DTNA is also betting on the full autonomous stack while closing the Portland plant (375 layoffs) and planning the largest US heavy-truck plant by 2029.

calls.heading: Confirm every software fix, per truck
Flag repeat repairs after each update
calls.sub: Find the trucks the fix missed.

calls.heading: Run freight for customers
calls.sub: Own the road, not just the truck.

booth.say: DTNA's challenge is seeing the cycle first: orders, chargers and warranties all send signals before the quarter does.
ask: How is tariff and pre-buy noise separated in the forecast?
Who owns telemetry data from 330,000 trucks today?
